newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex says Q1 crude, natgas output rose.
newsitem.headline: Pemex says Q1 crude, natgas output rose.

text.p: State oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said in a report on Tuesday that its crude exports for the first quarter averaged 1.613 million barrels per day (bpd), up from 1.484 million bpd in the same year-ago period.
Pemex also said its crude output averaged 2.958 million bpd, against 2.836 million bpd a year ago. In March Pemex saw crude production of 2.969 million bpd versus 2.869 million bpd in March 1996.
Output of natural gas averaged 4.347 billion cubic feet per day (cfd) for the first quarter, compared with 4.235 billion cfd during the first quarter of 1996.
For March, Pemex said its natural gas production was an average 4.392 billion cfd versus 4.257 billion cfd in the year-ago quarter.
Pemex exported 99.1 million cfd of natural gas in the first quarter, compared with imports of 48.9 million cfd. A year ago, Pemex exported 46.9 million cfd and imported 29.9 million cfd.
In the report, Pemex said its average price of exported crude rose 8.7 percent to $18.45 per barrel compared to the first quarter of 1996.
Pemex's pre-tax earnings during the quarter were 45.329 billion pesos, or $5.768 billion, up from a restated 35.716 billion pesos ($4.749 billion) during the year-ago quarter.

Pemex chairman Adrian Lajous told a news conference Pemex paid the federal government 41 billion pesos in taxes and rights during the quarter, an increase of 32 percent compared to the first three months of 1996.
